To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified five new genes that are expressed in the mouse male reproductive tract and belong to the protease inhibitor family of Kazal and WAP domains, and we have demonstrated that these genes are regulated by testosterone.
we have identified a group of protease inhibitors that is highly expressed in the epididymis and that we hypothesize to be important for sperm maturation.
we have discovered a novel family of five genes that encode epididymal-specific protease inhibitors with the Kazal or WAPI domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery and characterization of novel protease inhibitors with a Kazal or Wap domain that are highly expressed and specifically localized to the epithelial cells of the mouse epididyme.
the discovery and functional characterization of epididymis-specific protease inhibitors.
the discovery of novel epididymal proteins and their role in sperm maturation.

the novel genes identified in this study represent a group of genes that contribute to sperm maturation by controlling the proteolytic activity of the sperm surface.
these novel epididymal proteins may play a role in the regulation of epididymis function by regulating proteolytic activity in the epididymis and may be involved in male infertility.
these novel genes are likely to represent a group of genes that are involved in the regulation of spermatozoal maturation in the male reproductive tract and that they are regulated by testosterone.

we have identified a novel family of epididymosomes and their protease inhibitor content, and that these proteins may play a role in the regulation of sperm function.
